Prevention: Plant in the rainy season in clean soil
Select clean planting materials from parent plants.
Use tip of vines for planting since they are free of nematodes.
Farm sanitation - weeding, brushing, control burning and removal of debris.
Burn the trash on the surface of the bed to make hot fire for at least one hour.
The heat penetrates the soil and kills the nematode.
Loosen the soil to expose and desiccate nematodes
Do not apply fresh manure directly from the poultry because it might contain nematode
Apply hot water on the soil to treat small localised areas
Plant resistant varieties such as slipot
I-IV Solarise the soil using black tarpaulin.
The heat from the sun penetrates the soil and kills the nematode.
Monitoring: Check for stunted, poorly growing plants with yellowing leaves
Up-root some plants and observe roots for knots and balls made by the nematodes
Restrictions: Nematodes are difficult to control with nematicides and nematicides are not readily available in
MAFFS does not recommend attempting to use chemical controls on root-knot nematodes
